description: Current audit sign-offs. Each record classifies a claim, names its runtime implementation and dispatch evidence, and links executable tests (or an explicit not-tested status). Validated by scripts/validate-signoff.mjs via npm run repository:check.

records.claim: The exact pairwise CPU solver is the default runtime path and the parity reference for every approximate backend.
records.dispatch: Every law is gated with isSet(lawState, LAW_INDEXES.*) inside solve(); runtimeConfig.gravEngine defaults to the exact path.

records.claim: Barnes-Hut octree gravity is an opt-in approximate backend with a measured error envelope against the exact reference.
records.notes: Envelope measurements live in docs/BACKEND_ENVELOPES.md; exact solver remains the reference.

records.claim: The FMM cell evaluator is retained as an experimental opt-in backend; it is measured outside the shared error envelope and is never eligible to become the default backend.
records.dispatch: runtimeConfig.gravEngine === 'fmm' selects fmmGravity in solver.js; default remains exact.
records.notes: Decision recorded in docs/FEATURE_STATUS_MATRIX.md §3 and docs/BACKEND_ENVELOPES.md.

records.claim: WebGPU gravity compute is an opt-in backend with a deterministic CPU fallback contract.
records.dispatch: runtimeConfig.computeEngine === 'gpu' in physics.worker.js with GPU_FALLBACK on device failure; CONTACT/COLL stay CPU-owned.
records.notes: Hardware WebGPU parity remains an external-environment gate: the browser spec runs GPU-vs-CPU comparison when a device is granted and asserts bounded fallback when navigator.gpu is absent.

records.claim: Mechanics pair geometry is consolidated behind one shared scalar contract for diagnostics and orchestration consumers.
records.dispatch: getPairGeometry feeds mechanicsDiagnostics and tests; the solver hot path uses equivalent allocation-free local scalars documented as performance-specialized.

records.claim: Mechanics pair diagnostics are opt-in and side-effect free.
records.dispatch: inspectMechanicsPair is an explicit inspection utility; no solver gate consumes it by default.

records.claim: CONTACT performs geometric separation correction and stays distinct from impact impulse.
records.dispatch: isSet(lawState, LAW_INDEXES.CONTACT) gates the solver contact pass.

records.claim: COLL performs impact response as an operational proxy distinct from CONTACT geometry correction.
records.dispatch: isSet(lawState, LAW_INDEXES.COLL) gates the solver collision pass.

records.claim: The 136-law registry is a metadata catalogue; registry presence does not prove behavioral depth for each law.
The law relationship ontology is validated metadata with honestly reported coverage; it is descriptive evidence, never executable proof.
The 48-variant systems lifecycle registry is operational with deterministic topology, relationships, and replay reporting.
records.dispatch: Lifecycle serialization/restore is consumed by worldSave save/load flows.

records.claim: The renderer backend (PixiJS or Canvas2D) is user-selectable with automatic fallback when WebGL is unavailable.
records.dispatch: vepa-render-backend runtimeConfig selects the backend; renderer falls back to Canvas2D without WebGL.

records.claim: Audit stage provenance manifests are present and validated for every declared audit stage family.
Export snapshots follow a declared publication contract that is currently configured but not published.
records.notes: Validated by scripts/check-export-publication.mjs (npm run exports:check), not yet by an executable test — explicit evidence gap.

records.claim: Legacy runners and migration utilities are classified historical and excluded from active verification.
records.notes: Artifact inventory (npm run artifact:inventory) classifies scripts/patch-lawcat-test.mjs and tests/run.mjs as historical; they must never be invoked by CI or release gates.
